To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mice lacking the neurotrophin receptor TrkB in neural stem/progenitor cells in the hippocampus have impaired proliferation and differentiation of new neurons, and that they fail to respond to antidepressant treatment.

(i) TrkB regulates adult hippocampal neurogenis, (ii) TrkB is essential for the behavioral sensitivity to AD treatment, and (iii) the TrkB-mediated regulation of neurogenesis and behavioral responses to antidepressants occurs in a cell-autonomous manner in NPCs.

(1) mice lacking the receptor TrkB in adult hippocampal neural progenitor cells (aNPCs) display impaired proliferation and neurogenic potential; (2) aNPC-specific TrkB deletion also renders these mice refractory to antidepressant treatment; and (3) TrkB in mature DG neurons does not regulate proliferation or neurogenesis, and mice lacking TrkB in these cells respond normally to antidepressant treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the receptor tyrosin kinase TrkB in the regulation of hippocampal neuroplasticity.
the role of TrkB in regulating neurogenesis and antidepressive treatment sensitivity.

the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of adult hippocampal neurogenic processes, with a particular focus on the signaling pathways that are activated upon exposure to antidepressive treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TrkB signaling regulates adult neurogenesis and governs the sensitivity to ADs.
the absence of TrkB in NPCs leads to impaired proliferation and neurogenic differentiation, which in turn results in a behavioral response that is not affected by chronic antidepressant treatment.
the TrkB signaling pathway in NPCs is essential for proliferation and neuronal differentiation, and is required for the behavioral response to ADs and exercise in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TrkB is essential in NPCs for proliferation and differentiation.
TrkB is a critical regulator for adult hippocampal neurogenis and antidepressant response.
TrkB in NPCs is essential to regulate hippocampal neurogenic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that the receptor for brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) TrkB is essential for adult hippocampal neurogenic niche function.
TrkB in NPCs is essential for the regulation of adult hippocampal neurogenic activity and for the sensitivity to antidepressive treatment.

the receptor for brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) TrkB is a key regulator of adult neurogenesis and that its absence in neural progenitor cells (the cells that generate new neurons) is responsible for impaired neurogenesis and for behavioral insensitivity to antidepressive treatment.
